html:
The Tupinambá were Tupi-speaking peoples who lived along most of the coast of Brazil when the Portuguese arrived in 1500. They were the first Indigenous people of Brazil known to Europeans.

They lived in villages of large longhouses, farmed manioc and fished. Warfare between villages was central to their life, and captives were sometimes ritually killed and eaten, as the German gunner Hans Staden, their prisoner, described in 1557. They traded brazilwood with the Portuguese and French.

Disease, slave raids and wars destroyed most coastal groups within a century. Their language, as written down by the Jesuits, became the língua geral, the common language of colonial Brazil, spoken by settlers and bandeirantes into the 1700s. Many Brazilian place names, plants and animals have Tupi names. A modern Tupinambá community lives in Bahia.
sum: The Tupinambá were Tupi-speaking peoples who lived along most of the coast of Brazil when the Portuguese arrived in 1500. They were the first Indigenous people of Brazil known to Europeans.
